title: Select columns and aliases
summary: Select only the columns needed by the caller.
syntax:
SELECT expression AS output_name, other_column
FROM table_name AS alias;
rules: Select only the columns needed by the caller.
AS names an output column or table alias; double quotes delimit identifiers, single quotes delimit text.

title: Filter rows
summary: WHERE retains only rows where the predicate is true; unknown is excluded.
syntax:
SELECT columns FROM source
WHERE predicate AND (other_predicate OR fallback);
rules: WHERE retains only rows where the predicate is true; unknown is excluded.
Use parentheses to make AND/OR grouping clear; BETWEEN includes both endpoints.

title: Order and limit
summary: Without ORDER BY, row order is unspecified.
rules: Without ORDER BY, row order is unspecified.
Break ties with a unique key. NULL ordering differs by engine; use NULLS FIRST/LAST explicitly.

title: Join related tables
summary: INNER JOIN emits matching pairs; one customer can produce multiple order rows.
rules: INNER JOIN emits matching pairs; one customer can produce multiple order rows.
Qualify shared column names with table aliases and put the relationship in ON.

title: Find missing relationships
summary: LEFT JOIN preserves the left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.
syntax:
SELECT a.columns
FROM parent AS a
LEFT JOIN child AS b ON b.parent_id = a.id
WHERE b.id IS NULL;
rules: LEFT JOIN preserves the left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.
Test a non-nullable right-side key; a right-side filter in WHERE can accidentally remove unmatched parents.

title: Group totals and filter groups
summary: WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
syntax:
SELECT grouping_key, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM source
GROUP BY grouping_key
HAVING SUM(amount) > threshold;
rules: WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
Group every selected non-aggregate column for portable results. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) skips NULL.

title: NULL and three-valued logic
summary: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL; comparisons to NULL evaluate to unknown.
rules: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL; comparisons to NULL evaluate to unknown.
WHERE keeps true only. NOT unknown remains unknown; use NOT EXISTS instead of NOT IN when the set can contain NULL.

title: Subqueries and EXISTS
summary: EXISTS checks whether the subquery returns at least one row.
syntax:
SELECT p.columns FROM parent AS p
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM child AS c WHERE c.parent_id = p.id);
rules: EXISTS checks whether the subquery returns at least one row.
A correlated subquery references the outer row; NOT EXISTS safely handles nullable inner columns.

title: Common table expressions
summary: A CTE names a result within one statement; it is not a persistent table.
syntax:
WITH named_result AS (SELECT columns FROM source)
SELECT columns FROM named_result;
rules: A CTE names a result within one statement; it is not a persistent table.
Do not assume a CTE forces materialization or improves performance.

title: Window functions
summary: Window functions retain individual rows; GROUP BY collapses them.
rules: Window functions retain individual rows; GROUP BY collapses them.
ROW_NUMBER breaks ties using ORDER BY; RANK leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK does not. Use an explicit ROWS frame for running sums.

title: Insert rows
summary: List target columns explicitly; omitted columns use defaults or NULL when allowed.
syntax:
INSERT INTO table_name (column_a, column_b)
VALUES (value_a, value_b);
rules: List target columns explicitly; omitted columns use defaults or NULL when allowed.
A failed constraint rejects the statement; client code must still manage the surrounding transaction.

title: Update selected rows
summary: Omitting WHERE changes every row.
syntax: UPDATE table_name SET column = expression WHERE predicate;
rules: Omitting WHERE changes every row.
Inspect the predicate with SELECT and check the affected row count in your client.

title: Delete selected rows
summary: Omitting WHERE deletes every row.
syntax: DELETE FROM table_name WHERE predicate;
rules: Omitting WHERE deletes every row.
Foreign keys can reject a deletion; explicit transactions let you inspect changes before committing.

title: Keys and constraints
summary: PRIMARY KEY identifies rows; NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and foreign keys protect data invariants.
syntax:
CREATE TABLE table_name (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  code TEXT UNIQUE,
  amount INTEGER CHECK (amount >= 0),
  parent_id INTEGER REFERENCES parent(id)
);
rules: PRIMARY KEY identifies rows; NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and foreign keys protect data invariants.
SQLite foreign-key enforcement must be enabled on every connection; PostgreSQL enables it automatically. CHECK permits unknown, so add NOT NULL where needed.

title: Indexes and query plans
summary: Indexes can speed reads but add storage and write cost.
rules: Indexes can speed reads but add storage and write cost.
Column order matters in composite indexes; inspect real plans rather than assuming an index will be used.

title: Transactions and rollback
summary: COMMIT keeps changes; ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes. Use the same connection throughout.
rules: COMMIT keeps changes; ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes. Use the same connection throughout.
After an error PostgreSQL aborts the transaction until rollback (or rollback to an earlier savepoint); SQLite often aborts only the statement. Clients must explicitly recover.

title: Bound parameters
summary: Placeholders bind values, not table/column names. Pass parameters through the client API, never interpolate them into SQL.
rules: Placeholders bind values, not table/column names. Pass parameters through the client API, never interpolate them into SQL.
SQLite Python uses ? or :name; node-postgres and Go pgx use $1. A plain SQL console does not automatically bind these markers.

title: SQLite connection setup
summary: Enable foreign keys before opening a transaction on every SQLite connection.
rules: Enable foreign keys before opening a transaction on every SQLite connection.
Use exactly INTEGER PRIMARY KEY for a rowid alias. PostgreSQL uses identity columns instead.

title: PostgreSQL identity and RETURNING
summary: PostgreSQL identity generates a value from a sequence; a primary key also enforces uniqueness.
rules: PostgreSQL identity generates a value from a sequence; a primary key also enforces uniqueness.
RETURNING yields changed rows; sequence values may have gaps after rollback.

title: PostgreSQL upsert
summary: The conflict target needs a unique or exclusion constraint supported by the selected action.
syntax:
-- PostgreSQL only
INSERT INTO table_name (key, value) VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value
RETURNING key, value;
rules: The conflict target needs a unique or exclusion constraint supported by the selected action.
EXCLUDED contains the proposed row. This card documents PostgreSQL behavior even though SQLite has related syntax.

title: PostgreSQL JSONB
summary: JSONB stores parsed JSON; ->> extracts a JSON property as SQL text.
rules: JSONB stores parsed JSON; ->> extracts a JSON property as SQL text.
JSON null, missing keys and SQL NULL differ; PostgreSQL casts/operators do not transfer directly to SQLite JSON functions.
